subject: Future Tech
title: Printing in Space
description: Learn Printing in Space in one minute.

hook.text: In 2014, NASA sent a 3D printer to the International Space Station and printed a wrench 250 miles above Earth.

buildup.text: Sending a spare part from Earth takes months and costs $10,000 per pound.

discovery.text: Astronauts now print tools, replacement parts, and medical devices in orbit, designed on Earth and sent up as files.

twist.text: Relativity Space built Terran 1, a rocket where 85% of the structure was 3D-printed.

climax.text: Moon and Mars bases could 3D-print habitats from local regolith, avoiding the cost of shipping materials from Earth.

punchline.text: In space, the factory travels with you.

quiz.question: What was the first object 3D-printed on the International Space Station?
